category: Scripting system, process commands & the Altium Designer API
description: How Altium Designer is driven programmatically: script projects and the script editor, running scripts from the UI and from processes, the server-process command mechanism, and the PCB, schematic, workspace-manager and integrated-library object APIs with their factories, iterators and transaction wrappers.

tools.name: Scripting System overview
tools.description: Altium's built-in automation engine. It supports DelphiScript (the default and best supported), VBScript, JScript and legacy EnableBasic, running inside the application with access to a subset of the Delphi RTL, to script forms, and to the full Altium Designer API. Scripts can add dialogs, batch-edit designs, generate custom reports and drive any GUI command through a process string.
tools.usage: File > Run Script…; the Scripts panel; the script editor's Run command (F9)
tools.notes: The API reference on Altium's site was last fully updated for an older release, so verify interface members against the Script IDE's class browser before relying on them.

tools.name: Script Project (.PrjScr)
tools.description: The container for scripts: a script project groups script units (.pas, .vbs, .js, .bas) and script forms (.dfm) so that procedures can call each other and share forms. A script project must be open (or referenced by path) for the Run command and for the ScriptingSystem:RunScript process to find its procedures.
tools.usage: File > New > Project > Script Project; add units with right-click > Add New to Project > Script Unit / Script Form
tools.example: Create MyTools.PrjScr, add BoardTools.pas and a form BoardToolsForm.dfm, then File > Run Script > choose the procedure.

tools.name: Script units and script forms
tools.description: A script unit holds the procedures and functions; a script form is a visual dialog designed in the script editor's form designer with a paired .dfm layout file. Together they let a script present a real user interface with edit boxes, checkboxes and grids rather than a chain of ShowMessage prompts.
tools.usage: Right-click the script project > Add New to Project > Script Unit (.pas) / Script Form (.dfm + unit)
tools.example: Add a script form with a checkbox 'Add DRC violations' and a button, and handle the button's OnClick in the paired unit.

tools.name: Run Script (File > Run Script)
tools.description: Opens the Select Item To Run dialog, which browses scripts on the local disk, in a connected Workspace or among the open project documents, and lists the procedures each unit exposes. The chosen script stays loaded for the rest of the session, so it can be re-run quickly. This is the everyday way to run a script that is not part of the current design project.
tools.usage: File > Run Script… (DXP > Run Script in older releases)
tools.example: File > Run Script > browse to D:\scripts\MyTools.PrjScr > choose BoardTools.pas > ExportPadReport > Run.

tools.name: Script editor and debugging
tools.description: The script IDE: syntax-highlighted editor, the Run command (F9), breakpoints (click the gutter or Run > Toggle Breakpoint, F5), conditional breakpoints via Run > Add Breakpoint, single stepping, and watch/variable inspection. A running script halts at a breakpoint with the line highlighted so state can be inspected.
tools.usage: Open a script unit in the editor; Run > Run (F9), Run > Toggle Breakpoint (F5), Run > Add Breakpoint…, step commands on the Run menu
tools.example: Click the gutter beside the iterator loop to set a breakpoint, press F9, and inspect the component designator at each step.
tools.notes: Conditional breakpoints take an expression in the Add New Breakpoint dialog and only halt when it evaluates true.

tools.name: Scripts panel
tools.description: Lists the scripts available from the configured script locations (local folders and the connected Workspace) so they can be run without browsing. It is how a team publishes a shared set of tools: put the scripts in the Workspace and every engineer sees them in the panel.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Scripts; configure locations in Preferences > Scripting System
tools.example: Publish MyTools.PrjScr to the Workspace's Scripts folder; colleagues then run it straight from the Scripts panel.

tools.name: ResetParameters / AddStringParameter / RunProcess
tools.description: The parameter-stack mechanism for invoking a server process. `ResetParameters` clears the stack, `AddStringParameter` (and `AddIntegerParameter`, `AddWordParameter`, `AddBoolParameter`) push named values, and `RunProcess('Server:Command')` executes the command with them. Every Altium GUI command can be reached this way, which makes it the bridge between a script and functionality that has no object API.
tools.notes: Always call ResetParameters first: parameters left on the stack from a previous call are passed to the next process.

tools.name: Client.SendMessage
tools.description: Runs a process with all parameters in one pipe-separated string instead of using the parameter stack. It is equivalent to ResetParameters/RunProcess and is the more convenient form in VBScript and JScript, and for one-line commands. The third argument is the parameter-string length and the fourth is an optional target.
tools.usage: Client.SendMessage('<Server>:<Command>', '<param>=<value> | <param>=<value>', <length>, Nil);
tools.example: Client.SendMessage('WorkspaceManager:OpenObject', 'OpenMode=NewFromTemplate | ObjectKind=Project', 1024, Nil);

tools.name: Client object (OpenDocument / ShowDocument / CurrentView)
tools.description: The DXP platform object representing the running application. Beyond SendMessage it opens and shows documents (`Client.OpenDocument('PCB', path)` then `Client.ShowDocument(...)`), reports the current view and server, and gives access to the open document list. It is how a script switches the user to a particular schematic or PCB before acting on it.
tools.usage: Client.OpenDocument('<kind>', '<full path>'); Client.ShowDocument(<IServerDocument>); Client.CurrentView
tools.notes: Document kind strings are the server names, e.g. 'PCB', 'SCH', 'Text', 'PCBLIB', 'SCHLIB'.

tools.name: ScriptingSystem:RunScript
tools.description: The process that runs a named procedure in a named script unit of a named script project. It is what a custom menu item, toolbar button or keyboard shortcut is bound to when you want a script available without opening its project first, and it is how one script launches another.
tools.usage:
Process: ScriptingSystem:RunScript
Parameters: ProjectName=<path to .PrjScr>|ProcName=<unit.pas>><Procedure>
tools.example: ProjectName=C:\Users\Public\Documents\Altium\Delphiscript Scripts\General\HelloWorld.PRJSCR|ProcName=HelloWorld.pas>HelloWorld
tools.notes: For Workspace-hosted scripts use the script's 'Copy script parameters' command to get the correctly formatted path.

tools.name: ScriptingSystem:RunScriptText
tools.description: Executes a literal block of script statements passed as a parameter, rather than opening a script file. Useful for tiny one-liners wired to a toolbar button, and for generating behaviour at run time.
tools.usage:
Process: ScriptingSystem:RunScriptText
Parameters: Text=Begin <statements> End;
tools.example: Text=Begin RunApplication('notepad.exe'); End;

tools.name: RunApplication
tools.description: Launches an external program from a script. Paths containing spaces must be quoted inside the string. It is how a script hands off to a CAM viewer, a version-control client, a Python post-processor or a second copy of Altium Designer.
tools.usage: RunApplication('<full path or command>');
tools.example:
RunApplication('C:\Program Files\Altium\AD24\X2.EXE');
RunApplication('notepad.exe');

tools.name: PCBServer
tools.description: The entry point to the PCB API. `PCBServer.GetCurrentPCBBoard` returns the active board as an `IPCB_Board`; `PCBServer.GetPCBLibraryByPath` and `GetCurrentPCBLibrary` reach libraries; `PCBServer.PCBObjectFactory` creates new primitives; `PCBServer.PreProcess` and `PostProcess` bracket a set of edits into a single undoable transaction; `PCBServer.SendMessageToRobots` notifies the system that an object was created, changed or deleted so the display and DRC update.
tools.usage:
Board := PCBServer.GetCurrentPCBBoard;
PCBServer.PreProcess; … PCBServer.PostProcess;
tools.notes: Skipping PreProcess/PostProcess leaves the undo stack inconsistent; skipping SendMessageToRobots leaves the new object invisible to the display and the DRC until a refresh.

tools.name: IPCB_Board
tools.description: The board interface. It exposes the layer stack (`LayerStack`, `LayerIsInLayerStack`), the board outline (`BoardOutline`), the current layer, the origin, the board's components, nets, classes, rules and rooms, object creation via `AddPCBObject` / `RemovePCBObject`, iterators (`BoardIterator_Create`, `SpatialIterator_Create`), and the DRC entry points. Almost every PCB script starts by obtaining one.
tools.usage: Var Board : IPCB_Board; Board := PCBServer.GetCurrentPCBBoard;

tools.name: PCBServer.PCBObjectFactory
tools.description: Creates a new PCB primitive of a given object kind. The three arguments are the object type (eTrackObject, eArcObject, eViaObject, ePadObject, eTextObject, eFillObject, eRegionObject, ePolyObject, eComponentObject, eDimensionObject…), the dimension kind (eNoDimension for non-dimension objects) and the creation mode (eCreate_Default). The returned object is configured and then added to the board.
tools.usage: Obj := PCBServer.PCBObjectFactory(<object kind>, <dimension kind>, eCreate_Default);

tools.name: IPCB_BoardIterator
tools.description: Enumerates board objects. Create it with `Board.BoardIterator_Create`, narrow it with `AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(ePadObject, eViaObject))`, `AddFilter_LayerSet(AllLayers)` and `AddFilter_Method(eProcessAll)`, walk it with `FirstPCBObject` and `NextPCBObject`, and always release it with `Board.BoardIterator_Destroy(Iterator)`. A `SpatialIterator_Create` variant restricts the search to a rectangle.
tools.notes: Failing to destroy an iterator leaks it for the session; wrap the loop in try/finally where the language allows.

tools.name: IPCB_Track / IPCB_Arc / IPCB_Via / IPCB_Pad
tools.description: The routing and pad primitives. Tracks carry X1/Y1/X2/Y2, Width and Layer; arcs carry XCenter/YCenter, Radius, StartAngle/EndAngle and LineWidth; vias carry X/Y, Size, HoleSize, LowLayer/HighLayer and their mask expansions; pads carry Name (designator), X/Y, Layer, the per-layer size and shape, HoleSize, HoleType and Rotation. All of them expose Net, Component and the Selected/Moveable flags.
tools.usage: Track.Width := MilsToCoord(12); Pad.HoleSize := MMsToCoord(0.9); Via.LowLayer := eTopLayer;
tools.notes: Modifying an existing object must be bracketed by PCBM_BeginModify / PCBM_EndModify messages or the change is not registered for undo and DRC.

tools.name: IPCB_Component
tools.description: A placed footprint. It exposes Name (the designator text object), Comment, Pattern (footprint name), SourceDesignator and SourceLibReference, x/y position, Rotation, Layer (which side it is on), Moveable/Locked, and a group iterator (`GroupIterator_Create`) over its own primitives — pads, tracks, 3D bodies and text.
tools.usage: Comp.Name.Text, Comp.Comment.Text, Comp.Pattern, Comp.x, Comp.y, Comp.Rotation, Comp.Layer

tools.name: Coordinate conversion helpers
tools.description: The PCB API stores coordinates in internal units, so every geometric value must be converted: `MilsToCoord`/`CoordToMils` and `MMsToCoord`/`CoordToMMs` convert in each direction, and `CoordUnitToString` formats a value for display in the board's current unit. Forgetting the conversion produces objects that are microscopically small or absurdly large.
tools.usage: Track.Width := MilsToCoord(10); mm := CoordToMMs(Pad.HoleSize);
tools.example: ShowMessage('Hole = ' + CoordUnitToString(Pad.HoleSize, eMetric));

tools.name: SchServer
tools.description: The entry point to the schematic API. `SchServer.GetCurrentSchDocument` returns the active `ISch_Document`; `SchServer.GetSchDocumentByPath` opens one by path; `SchServer.SchObjectFactory` creates new schematic objects; `SchServer.ProcessControl.PreProcess` / `PostProcess` bracket a set of edits for undo; and `SchServer.RobotManager.SendMessage` notifies the system of creation and modification.
tools.usage:
Doc := SchServer.GetCurrentSchDocument;
SchServer.ProcessControl.PreProcess(Doc, ''); … SchServer.ProcessControl.PostProcess(Doc, '');

tools.name: ISch_Document
tools.description: A schematic sheet. It exposes the sheet size, style and border, the document's parameters, object creation through `RegisterSchObjectInContainer` and removal through `RemoveSchObject`, iterators (`SchIterator_Create`), and `GraphicallyInvalidate` to force a redraw after programmatic edits.
tools.usage: Doc.RegisterSchObjectInContainer(Obj); Doc.GraphicallyInvalidate;

tools.name: ISch_Iterator
tools.description: Enumerates schematic objects. `Doc.SchIterator_Create` makes one, `AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(eSchComponent))` narrows it to a class of objects, `FirstSchObject`/`NextSchObject` walk it, and `Doc.SchIterator_Destroy(Iter)` releases it. A component has its own `SchIterator_Create` for walking its pins and parameters.
tools.usage: Iter := Doc.SchIterator_Create; Iter.AddFilter_ObjectSet(MkSet(eSchComponent)); … Doc.SchIterator_Destroy(Iter);

tools.name: ISch_Component / ISch_Pin / ISch_Parameter
tools.description: The schematic component and its members. `ISch_Component` exposes Designator and Comment (as text objects with a Text property), LibReference, DesignItemId, CurrentPartID, Location, Orientation and its parameter and pin collections; `ISch_Pin` gives Designator, Name, Electrical type and Location; `ISch_Parameter` gives Name, Value and visibility.
tools.usage: Cmp.Designator.Text, Cmp.Comment.Text, Cmp.LibReference, Pin.Designator, Param.Name / Param.Value

tools.name: ISch_Wire and schematic object factory
tools.description: Wires, net labels, ports, junctions and every other schematic primitive are created with `SchServer.SchObjectFactory(<object id>, eCreate_Default)` — object ids include eWire, eNetLabel, ePort, eJunction, eSchComponent, ePowerObject, eParameter, eLabel. A wire's geometry is built by setting its vertex list before registering it in the document.
tools.usage: Obj := SchServer.SchObjectFactory(<eObjectId>, eCreate_Default); … Doc.RegisterSchObjectInContainer(Obj);

tools.name: Workspace Manager API (GetWorkspace / IProject / IDocument)
tools.description: The project-level API. `GetWorkspace` returns the `IWorkspace`; `DM_FocusedProject` and `DM_Projects(i)` give `IProject` objects; `DM_Compile` validates a project; `DM_LogicalDocuments`/`DM_PhysicalDocuments` enumerate its documents as `IDocument`; and the compiled model exposes buses, nets, components and pins for netlist and report generation.
tools.usage: WS := GetWorkspace; Prj := WS.DM_FocusedProject; Prj.DM_Compile; Doc := Prj.DM_LogicalDocuments(i);
tools.notes: Call DM_Compile before reading nets or components, or the compiled model is empty or stale.

tools.name: Netlist generation from a script
tools.description: The shipped ScripterProtelNetlist example shows the pattern: open the script project, compile the design project through the Workspace Manager API, walk the compiled nets and their pins, and write a netlist file into the project's Generated folder. It is the template for any custom export format a downstream tool requires.
tools.usage: Open ScripterProtelNetlist.PRJSCR > File > Run Script > ScripterProtelNetlist.pas
tools.example:
1. Open the ScripterProtelNetlist.PRJSCR example project.
2. Focus the design project whose netlist you want.
3. File > Run Script > ScripterProtelNetlist.pas; the netlist appears in the project's Generated folder.

tools.name: Shipped script examples
tools.description: Altium installs a large example collection organised by API area: the DXP folder demonstrates the Client and system API, PCB the PCB API, Sch the schematic API, WSM the Workspace Manager API, Processes the server processes, and General the DelphiScript language itself. Named examples include Count_pads, CountTracksInComponent, IterateNets, IterateComponentBodies, Layers_Info, QueryLayerStack, QueryLayerPairs, QueryMechLayers and ScripterProtelNetlist.
tools.usage: \Examples\Scripts\DelphiScript Scripts\{DXP, PCB, Sch, WSM, Processes, General} under the Altium documents folder
tools.example: Open \Examples\Scripts\DelphiScript Scripts\PCB\PCB_Scripts.PRJSCR and run Count_pads against an open board.
tools.notes: Some legacy examples no longer run unmodified because the API has changed; they remain useful as structural references.

tools.name: Altium GitHub script collection
tools.description: Altium maintains a public collection of community and official scripts covering pad and via reports, layer stack export, net auditing, silkscreen repositioning, BOM helpers and more. It is the practical starting point for a new script because working, current examples are more reliable than the older shipped set.
tools.usage: Browse the Altium Designer scripts collection on GitHub; clone the .PrjScr and run it with File > Run Script
tools.example: Clone the collection, open the desired .PrjScr, and adapt the closest example rather than starting from a blank unit.

tools.name: Process command reference (Server:Command strings)
tools.description: Every Altium command exists as a `Server:Command` string with documented parameters: the PCB server (PCB:Zoom, PCB:Select, PCB:DeSelect, PCB:PlaceVia, PCB:InteractiveRoute, PCB:SwitchTo2D/SwitchTo3D, PCB:DRC), the Sch server (Sch:Zoom, Sch:PlacePart, Sch:Select, Sch:DeSelect, Sch:Annotate), the Workspace Manager (WorkspaceManager:OpenObject, WorkspaceManager:Compile, WorkspaceManager:GenerateReport) and the Client itself. The Process Parameters Reference in the online help lists them.
tools.usage: ResetParameters; AddStringParameter('<param>','<value>'); RunProcess('<Server>:<Command>');
tools.notes: Parameter names and accepted values are per command; check the Process Parameters Reference rather than guessing, and test interactively before scripting.

tools.name: Custom menus, toolbars and shortcuts for scripts
tools.description: A script becomes a first-class command by binding `ScriptingSystem:RunScript` to a menu item, toolbar button or keyboard shortcut through the Customize dialog. This is what turns a useful script into part of the everyday workflow instead of something reached through a file browser.
tools.usage: Right-click a toolbar > Customize… > New… > Process: ScriptingSystem:RunScript, Parameters: ProjectName=…|ProcName=…>…, assign a caption, icon and shortcut
tools.example: Add a PCB toolbar button 'Pad Report' running ScriptingSystem:RunScript with the parameters pointing at PadReport.pas>PadReport.

tools.name: DelphiScript language notes
tools.description: DelphiScript implements a subset of Delphi: it is case-insensitive except inside string literals, has no strong typing for script variables declared with Var, supports procedures, functions, records, arrays and classes from the supported RTL subset, and uses `MkSet`/`SetUnion` helpers in place of Delphi set literals for API filters. Forms are created at run time from the paired .dfm.
tools.usage: Var … Begin … End; with Delphi syntax; MkSet(eTrackObject, eArcObject) for API object sets
tools.notes: Array-of-set arguments in the API must be built with MkSet/SetUnion; a Delphi-style `[eTrackObject]` literal is not accepted.

tools.name: VBScript and JScript support
tools.description: Scripts can also be written in VBScript (.vbs) and JScript (.js), which reach the same API objects and processes. The main practical differences are the absence of the Delphi RTL helpers, a clumsier parameter-stack syntax (favouring Client.SendMessage), and weaker community example coverage — most published Altium scripts are DelphiScript.
tools.usage: Add a Script Unit and choose the VBScript or JScript language; run the same way with File > Run Script
tools.example:
' VBScript
RunProcess "PCB:SwitchTo2D"
tools.notes: Prefer DelphiScript for new work: it is the default, the best documented and the language of the shipped and community examples.

tools.name: Altium Designer SDK / DXP extensions
tools.description: For behaviour that scripting cannot reach — new document editors, persistent panels, custom servers, compiled performance — Altium provides an SDK for building DXP extensions in Delphi (and C# for newer extension types). Extensions register servers, processes, panels and menu items with the platform and are distributed and installed through Extensions and Updates.
tools.usage: Obtain the SDK for the target Altium Designer version; implement and register the server; package as an installable extension
tools.example:
1. Build the extension against the matching SDK version.
2. Register its processes and panel.
3. Install via Extensions and Updates > from local file.
tools.notes: SDK availability and the supported languages vary by release and licence; confirm with Altium before committing to this route.

tools.name: Command-line launch of Altium Designer
tools.description: Altium Designer is started as `X2.EXE`, optionally with a project or document path so it opens directly on that design — the behaviour the DXP protocol handler and Altium 365's 'Open in Altium Designer' rely on. There is no publicly documented switch for running a script or generating outputs headlessly; automation is done from inside the application through the scripting system and OutJobs.
tools.usage: X2.EXE ["<path to .PrjPcb / .SchDoc / .PcbDoc>"]
tools.example: "C:\Program Files\Altium\AD24\X2.EXE" "D:\work\sensor_board\sensor_board.PrjPcb"
tools.notes: Command-line switches of the form -RScriptFile/-RScriptProc circulate in forums but are not documented by Altium; treat them as unverified and prefer ScriptingSystem:RunScript from inside the application.
